CERSAI Mortgage Report in Hyderabad

An equitable mortgage created by depositing title deeds may never appear in the EC. A CERSAI search reveals the bank and NBFC charges hiding on a property.

Key Takeaways

  • CERSAI is the central registry where banks and NBFCs record security interests (mortgages) on property.
  • Equitable mortgages — created by deposit of title deeds — often do NOT appear in the Encumbrance Certificate.
  • A CERSAI search reveals lenders' registered charges that an EC alone can miss.
  • Buying a mortgaged property means the lender can enforce its charge against you.
  • We run the CERSAI check as part of proper pre-purchase due diligence.

One of the most dangerous gaps in property due diligence is the equitable mortgage — a loan a bank grants against the original title deeds without a registered mortgage deed. Because nothing is registered at the SRO, it may not show up in the EC at all.

CERSAI is the national registry created to close exactly this gap. JaaGa runs a CERSAI search so you know whether any lender has an active charge on the property.

When You Need a CERSAI Check

Before buying any property, alongside the EC — especially resale flats and properties the seller once used to raise a loan.

Whenever the seller has, or previously had, a home loan, business loan or loan against property.

How We Run the CERSAI Search

  1. 1

    Collect Property & Owner Data

    We take the property address/details and owner identity information needed for the registry search.

  2. 2

    Search the Registry

    We query CERSAI for registered security interests against the property and owner.

  3. 3

    Interpret Any Charge

    We identify the lender, the type of charge and whether it is active or satisfied.

  4. 4

    You receive a clear statement of any registered mortgage and what it means for the purchase.

Documents Required

  • Property address and details
  • Owner name and identity details
  • Existing title document

Common Problems We Solve

EC looks clean, loan exists

Equitable mortgages bypass the SRO. The CERSAI search is what surfaces them.

Charge not marked satisfied

Some closed loans remain shown as active. We help confirm and clear the status.

Multiple lenders

Properties can carry more than one charge. We report all of them, not just the first.

Why CERSAI Mortgage Report Matters

If you buy a property that carries an unsatisfied mortgage, the lender's right to recover the loan can follow the property to you. A CERSAI report — paired with the EC — is how you make sure the home you're buying isn't already the bank's collateral.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is CERSAI?

The Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest — a national registry where lenders record mortgages and charges on property.

Why isn't the mortgage in the EC?

Equitable mortgages are created by depositing title deeds without registering a mortgage deed at the SRO, so they may not reflect in the EC. CERSAI captures them.

Should I do both EC and CERSAI?

Yes. They cover different risks — the EC covers registered transactions, CERSAI covers lenders' security interests. Together they give a fuller picture.

Can a closed loan still show?

Sometimes the charge isn't marked satisfied even after repayment. We help identify and resolve this.

Can NRIs use this service?

Yes, entirely remotely — share the details on WhatsApp and we handle the search.
